sentences.text: Shri Eshaan Datt, learned counsel for the appellant.
Shri Pramod Pandey- Govt. Advocate for the State.
Applicant/appellant Dheeraj Badele seeks suspension of sentence during the pendency of present criminal appeal.
He has been convicted and sentenced to undergo RI for 20 years with a fine of Rs.3,000/- under Section 5-L/6 of POCSO Act in place of Sections 376(2)(n) and 376(3) of IPC with default stipulations.
The prosecution story started with the allegations that the victim No.1(U) was studying in 7th Class and the victim No.2(K) was her cousin as well as friend.
The victim No.1 was introduced to the applicant/appellant by the victim No.2.
The allegations were made that the applicant/appellant committed rape upon the victims.
On 23.10.2019 the victim No.2 told the victim No.1 now it would be known as to whom the applicant/appellant was loving.
On being asked, the applicant/appellant denied loving either of the two.
On this the victim No.2 exhorted that it would be better to die and resultantly she jumped into a well.
The trial Court has acquitted the applicant/appellant qua his complicity viz- a-viz the victim No.2, as the scientific tests were found to be in negation to the allegations.

Learned counsel for the applicant/appellant submits that dehors the age determination as per the provisions of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act of 2015, the complicity of the applicant/appellant in respect of commission of offence under Section 376 of IPC upon the victim No.1 has not 2 CRA-2230-2023 been established by way of any scientific mechanism.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act of 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As per the DNA profile (Ex.P-30), very low un-interpretable Y-chromosome STR DNA profile were found.

The DNA report negated the theory of rape upon the victim No.1, however the trial Court proceeded to record the conviction of the applicant/appellant solely on the basis of her age, which was found to be 13 years 13 days.
Learned counsel for the applicant/appellant submits that though the age of the victim No.1 was not determined as per the established principle of law.

In view of the DNA profile,
the allegations of rape could not be proved, and therefore the applicant/appellant deserves to be granted concession of suspension of sentence even qua his complicity viz-a-viz the victim No.1.
Per contra, learned State counsel opposed the prayer on the premise that the allegation of rape was found proved as per the testimony of the victim and the victim was found to be minor.
The applicant/appellant has rightly been convicted in view of Section 305 of IPC.

sentences.text: Taking into consideration the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case particularly in the light of the DNA report (Ex.P-30) and also in view of the period already undergone by the applicant/appellant, we deem it appropriate to suspend the remaining sentence of the applicant/appellant, subject to his furnishing a personal bail bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety bond in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Chief Judicial Magistrate concerned with a further direction to appear before the trial Court concerned on 16.10.2024 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard, during the pendency of this appeal.
Accordingly, aforesaid application is allowed.
